title: Preemptive chaos playbook: GPU-pool saturation, region ejection, and external dependency blackholes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Validate Redwood inference behavior when faced with three concurrent failure modes: full GPU pool exhaustion in a single region, control-plane simulated region loss (routing blackhole), and an external dependency blackhole (model-store/kv/metrics). The goal is to ensure SLOs degrade gracefully, circuit breakers and load-shedding policies engage correctly, fallbacks route to healthy pools and regions, and runbooks + alerts are actionable. This ticket captures the experiment plan, safety constraints, measurable acceptance criteria, and follow-ups for production hardening.
acceptance_criteria: When a single region's GPU pool reaches 95% utilization and then becomes unresponsive, 99th-percentile tail latency across global requests must not exceed configured regional-SLO multiplier more than 3x baseline for longer than 5 minutes
Circuit breaker should trip for the affected pool within 30s of consistent 500s/timeout errors and prevent >80% of new requests from routing to the failed pool
Traffic routed away from the failed region must not increase error rate in fallback region above a pre-agreed spike threshold (customer_impact: medium) for more than 10 minutes
Load-shedding policies (token-bucket / priority queues) must drop low-priority background evals instead of user traffic in >95% of trials
Automated rollback and re-routing playbook verified end-to-end (playbook step executed, incident timer recorded, notification channels validated)
experiment_plan: Phase 0 - Safety and staging: Run entire suite in 'staging' cluster with realistic traffic replay for 2 hours and validate telemetry. Confirm canary flags and kill-switch toggles work.

Phase 1 - GPU pool pressure: Gradually inject artificial allocation pressure in us-west-2 GPU pool by launching synthetic inference traffic that emulates 75/90/100% utilization bands. Wait 10 minutes at each band and observe autoscaler and scheduling behavior.

Phase 2 - Controlled ejection: After sustained 100% utilization, flip a simulated 'pool-unavailable' switch (API-based ejection) to emulate kernel-level exhaustion and network stall to that pool. Observe circuit breaker states and routing policy execution.

Phase 3 - Dependency blackhole: Simultaneously throttle outbound connections from the serving runtime to the model-store/kv and to downstream metrics ingestion for 3 minutes to create a blackhole condition, then restore.

Phase 4 - Region loss: Simulate control-plane partition in one region (route table blackhole) using chaos toolkit to remove the region from service-discovery for 5 minutes, forcing cross-region rerouting and validating shard re-assignment and KV cache behavior.
Phase 5 - Recovery and post-mortem: Reintroduce systems, run smoke checks, collect full telemetry, and perform post-mortem within 72 hours. Capture regression tests and policy tuning required.
safety_controls: Run only during maintenance window: Tue/Wed 02:00-05:00 UTC unless explicitly authorized
Start in staging and then isolated production namespace with 5% of traffic routed through experiment ring (gradual canary) before full production simulation
Kill-switch endpoints: /chaos/abort & /chaos/pause monitored by SRE oncall. Manual abort triggers immediate teardown and automated rollback of routing configs.

Max blast radius: single region and a small set of non-critical customer tenants (preselected low-impact workspaces). No experiments targeting enterprise production customers without account-level opt-in.
Escalation path: SRE oncall -> Head of Site Reliability -> PagerDuty #prod-incident, and Slack #resilience for live updates
